How do we figure out what size AC you need

Sizing is not guesswork. Bigger is not always better. An oversized system can cool fast but leave the air feeling clammy, or cycle on and off more than you would like. An undersized system may struggle on warmer afternoons. To understand the basics of cooling loads, you can review background information on air conditioning.

We look at items like

  • Square footage and ceiling height
  • Window size and sun exposure
  • Insulation and attic conditions
  • Number of occupants and typical daily activity
  • Existing duct size and layout if you have ducts
  • Equipment placement options and airflow paths

A simple example is a two story townhome with a warm upstairs may need zoning or targeted airflow changes, not just a stronger unit. Sometimes the fix is partly equipment choice and partly duct corrections such as Air Duct Maintenance in La Jolla Mesa, CA.

Yes. If your La Jolla Mesa home or workspace does not have ducts, ductless mini splits are often a clean route. Cooling results depend on more than the equipment itself. The system can be installed correctly and still feel limited if the building is fighting it. Common factors in La Jolla Mesa properties include sun exposure through large windows and sliders, older insulation, air leaks around doors and attic penetrations, duct layout that does not match a remodeled floor plan, ceiling fans that help but also show where air is not moving well, and thermostat placement near kitchens or sunny hallways.

We will talk through what we see. Sometimes the best next step is sealing a few key leaks or improving return airflow. It is usually physical and fixable, just not always in one single step.
